title: fix: allow keyless retries for cached media generations
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves the `/v1/images/generations` cache lookup before generation access checks.
- Lets an identical keyless retry receive completed cached media after the original client disconnects.
- Keeps cache misses behind the existing authentication, permission, balance, deduplication, and billing path.
- Extends the existing full-route test to replay a cached POST without its original API key.

Tests: `npx vitest run test/index.test.ts`; `npx vitest run test/openai-image-cache.test.ts`; `npm run typecheck`

gist.headline: Second buzz, same pixels
gist.blurb: Sometimes a client flies away just before the picture arrives. Now an identical retry can collect the finished cached media without bringing its original API key back to the garden.
gist.summary: Moved the `/v1/images/generations` cache lookup ahead of generation access checks, so identical keyless retries can retrieve completed cached media while cache misses still follow authentication, permissions, balance, deduplication, and billing.
gist.impact: If a client disconnects after starting an image generation, retrying the same request can now receive its completed cached result instead of needing the original API key, while new generations remain protected by the existing access path.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy delivery-retry scene: Polli helps a small retro terminal recover a finished pixel image from a cache jar after its connection string has snapped. The completed artwork is safely waiting on a lime-green shelf, while code-plants and flowers reinforce that only the already-grown result is being collected.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, black antennae and oval eyes, bright pink rectangular cheek blush, tiny smile, and rounded light-blue translucent wings, wearing a tiny mail carrier cap as she hands a completed pixel landscape from a glowing cache jar to a friendly retro terminal with a loose unplugged cable. Lime green (#ecf874) appears prominently on the cache shelf and terminal glow, with code-plants, small flowers, warm cream and lavender pastels, subtle CRT scanlines, and pixel-font text reading “CACHED”. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes; nostalgic, emotionally warm, like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike.
